newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity prices up with strong physicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity prices up with strong physicals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Thursday, riding on the coattails of stronger physical power prices in the U.S. West, industry sources said.
"Cash was screaming higher again this morning," said one New York-based futures trader.
But sources said the higher power futures trade was based on relatively thin volume, and several looked for a price downturn soon based on the return to service of two California nuclear power units.

As of 1250 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) was trading up $1.18 at $35.85 per megawatt hour (MWh) following trades at $35.35-35.95, while September was up 52 cents at $28.90 after trades at $28.65-29.10 per MWh.
August California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up 48 cents at $22.10 following exchanges at $22.00-22.25, while September was up 24 cents at the day's low of $22.05 from a high of $22.15 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1210 an estimated total of 293 PV and 39 COB contracts had traded.
Sources said next-day peak physical power at Palo Verde had traded as high as $55.00 Thursday morning from $44.00-47.00 on Wednesday for Thursday delivery.
The higher prices came despite several power plants being set to return to service, led by the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) units in California.
The 1,070 megawatt (MW) SONGS unit 2, in San Clemente, Calif., was operating at 70 percent of capacity as of Thursday morning and was scheduled to reach full output sometime today.
The adjoining 1,080 MW SONGS unit 3 was scheduled to be placed on line today.
In Richland, Washington, output at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant achieved 87 percent early Thursday.
The 750 MW Mohave coal-fired unit 3 was shut Monday for repairs and expected to resume operations Saturday, while the 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming may restart today.
The 254 MW Valmy coal-fired unit 1 in Nevada was unlikely to return to full power until the weekend, after its output was halved Tuesday because of a tube leak.
Forecasters called for normal temperatures to continue across the Pacific Northwest into next week, and hot but seasonal weather over most of the Southwest.
Separately, southbound capacity on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie transmission system was set to be cut by 250 MW to 3,200 MW between 0900 and 1600 PDT today and Friday for maintenance work.
As of 1250 EDT, August NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up 0.6 cents at $2.18 per million British thermal units.
